{"task": {"id": "I_kwDOVRCof88AAAABZivgHg", "item_id": "PVTI_lAHOAHSLSM4Bn7ElzhDJhIE", "project_id": "PVT_kwHOAHSLSM4Bn7El", "number": 81, "title": "Confirm and fix BIOS floppy DMA handoff after SPECIFY ND=1", "body": "## Problem

**Suspected regression requiring Coordinator reproduction:** after a guest selects FDC non-DMA mode, synthetic BIOS floppy transfers still assume DMA without selecting it. Static analysis predicts failed BIOS reads and rejected writes on both VM and Ap. This affects software mixing direct controller access with BIOS storage services; no commercial compatibility failure has been demonstrated.

The source change is [PR #80](https://github.com/takahirox/pc98-rust/pull/80), resolving #79, merged as [`14824332666e7a7ce3a529d766a7af282865f23e`](https://github.com/takahirox/pc98-rust/commit/14824332666e7a7ce3a529d766a7af282865f23e). The preceding baseline is `ae6b96926ce9146de9dbdfd1269686b74ae3a643`.

## Expected outcome

From an idle controller with ND=1, BIOS floppy reads and writes establish DMA mode through the normal controller command interface before transferring data. They complete through the existing FDC/DMA path, report the existing BIOS status contract, and leave the controller usable for subsequent commands.

Preserve PR #80's intended capability: raw clients can issue SPECIFY ND=1 and perform supported byte-handshaked PIO reads, including after a BIOS transfer. BIOS setup may select ND=0; preserving ND=1 across BIOS calls is not required.

Hardware semantics:

- SPECIFY is `03h`, followed by SRT/HUT and HLT/ND; ND is bit 0 of the final byte. ND=1 selects non-DMA operation and ND=0 selects DMA. SPECIFY has no execution or result phase. See [NEC µPD765A/B, Table 4, PDF page 15](https://hxc2001.com/download/datasheet/floppy/thirdparty/FDC/NEC/UPD765_Datasheet_OCRed.pdf#page=15) and [NEC Application Note 8, PDF page 26](https://hxc2001.com/download/datasheet/floppy/thirdparty/FDC/NEC/uPD765_App_Note_Mar79.pdf#page=26).
- MSR RQM/DIO govern register access; EXM distinguishes non-DMA execution. Data bytes must not be mistaken for result bytes. See [NEC µPD765A/B, Table 2, PDF page 9](https://hxc2001.com/download/datasheet/floppy/thirdparty/FDC/NEC/UPD765_Datasheet_OCRed.pdf#page=9).

The BIOS setup policy above is a synthetic-firmware contract, not a claim about proprietary NEC BIOS internals.

## Context and reproduction

Source evidence at the recorded merge:

- [src/bus.rs](https://github.com/takahirox/pc98-rust/blob/14824332666e7a7ce3a529d766a7af282865f23e/src/bus.rs#L890) retains ND at line 896. Lines 924–965 reject unsupported ND commands, including writes, or enter delayed PIO reads.
- [firmware::disk_transfer](https://github.com/takahirox/pc98-rust/blob/14824332666e7a7ce3a529d766a7af282865f23e/src/firmware.rs#L78) programs channel-2 DMA, submits READ/WRITE DATA and reads supposed results after 160 clocks, without issuing SPECIFY. This file was unchanged by PR #80. The INT 1Bh transfer services call this helper.
- [tests/fdc.rs](https://github.com/takahirox/pc98-rust/blob/14824332666e7a7ce3a529d766a7af282865f23e/tests/fdc.rs#L298) explicitly sends `03 DF 02` before testing restored DMA. [tests/core.rs](https://github.com/takahirox/pc98-rust/blob/14824332666e7a7ce3a529d766a7af282865f23e/tests/core.rs#L406) tests BIOS transfers from default DMA state. Neither covers BIOS taking over an idle ND=1 controller.

Coordinator reproduction, using original patterned media:

1. On each profile, enable the DMA controller and mount a writable supported floppy. Send `03 DF 03` through port `0092h`, advance command dispatch, and confirm idle MSR.
2. Without clearing ND or resetting, request one valid 1,024-byte BIOS read into guarded RAM. Independently repeat from fresh state for a BIOS write with a distinct payload.
3. Exercise both the helper and an actual guest INT 1Bh: AL=`90h`, AH=`06h` for read or `05h` for write, CH=3, CL=cylinder, DH=head, DL=sector, BX=1,024, ES:BP=buffer.
4. Record return status, payload/media differences, DMA progression and FDC phase. Compare the same minimal reproduction at the preceding baseline and recorded merge. Expected success is CF clear/AH=0 with exact data; the present failure prediction remains unconfirmed until executed.

Progress assessment: the Coordinator reports 324 native tests and 110 production release-Wasm browser cases passing for PR #80, with existing regressions preserved; the default browser attempt ran zero cases because its port was occupied. See [recorded validation](https://github.com/takahirox/pc98-rust/blob/14824332666e7a7ce3a529d766a7af282865f23e/docs/validation.md#issue-79-fdc-non-dma-read-data). Independent PR review and remote CI evidence were not supplied. This evaluator inspected source/diffs and specifications only; it ran no builds/tests or fixture preparation and made no changes.

All 26 inventory categories retain their supplied scopes and statuses: paging and FPU are unimplemented, GRCG is implemented_unverified, and the other 23 categories are partial. None is verified. Limited probes and six-game reports do not establish full hardware accuracy or commercial compatibility. Protected mode, paging and basic x87 remain required.

Scope is the idle-controller BIOS/FDC mode handoff. FDC remains partial: PIO writes, multi-track, deleted-data/format/scan, N=0/DTL, fuller SPECIFY timing, board/error behavior, additional media coverage and 512-byte IPL acceptance remain outstanding. Active-command preemption, BIOS VERIFY redesign, unrelated hardware work and game research are non-goals. No duplicate open Issue is listed in the supplied context.

## Pre-merge acceptance criteria

- [ ] First reproduce and confirm or refute the suspected regression using original tests on the exact merge and preceding baseline. Record commands and observed differences. If the prediction is refuted, investigate only this handoff and document the evidence and concrete fix/no-regression decision.
- [ ] For a confirmed regression, implement the smallest forward fix that selects DMA through the normal FDC command path and waits for command readiness. Document the synthetic BIOS's SPECIFY parameters. Do not bypass sector transfer through direct media copying or disable retained ND/PIO behavior.
- [ ] Add original Rust regressions for both profiles: ND=1 followed independently by BIOS read and write, same-cylinder and seek-required requests, exact payloads, guarded buffers, complete expected media differences, DMA address/count/terminal-count behavior, drained results and subsequent command usability. Retain missing-sector and write-protection error behavior.
- [ ] Add an original source-built guest probe with license, build command, hashes, independent expected results and an explicit execution budget. Through actual INT 1Bh, cover ND=1 → BIOS read/write and completed PIO read → BIOS transfer → fresh SPECIFY ND=1 → PIO read. Assert CF/AH, payloads, guards and exact intended media writes. Host code only mounts, steps, observes and resets.
- [ ] Run the identical guest image natively and through production release-Wasm on VM/Ap, before/after reset and at both `/` and `/pc98-rust/`. Require bounded completion and no guest/core/browser errors.
- [ ] Coordinator runs `cargo test --locked --test fdc --test core --test dma --test pic`, full `cargo test --locked`, `cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings`, `cargo fmt --check`, `git diff --check`, and the README's production Wasm/browser checks. Preserve existing PIO, DOS/apps/VM/audio, IDE-edge and six-game assertions and budgets. Use original or licensed source-built acceptance probes with explicit provenance; acquire no commercial ROMs or guest software. Report failures, skipped checks and actual browser case counts honestly; port-only overrides must preserve both serving paths and assertions.
- [ ] Record reproduction, final validation and review evidence in the PR. If a confirmed severe regression cannot receive a safe bounded fix, explicitly justify rollback, inspect dependent changes, and use a normal reviewed revert PR targeting merge `14824332666e7a7ce3a529d766a7af282865f23e` with the appropriate mainline parent. Do not rewrite history or report a revert before it occurs. Implementation, execution, review and merge belong to the resident Coordinator.

## Optional validation

None.

## Required post-merge verification

None.
